column2: For those who live thus there is no return again; there exists, through imperishability, another, beyond, the undecaying.
Those of one mind would see him; right seeing is not in them; they reach the unmanifest again and again, scourge of foes.
Knowing all this, but not by awakening all, they will become manifest, following the manifest.
All is said to be the unmanifest; the twenty-fifth is not all; those who know him have no fear.
[Vasishtha said:] "They call the unmanifest ignorance, subject to the law of creation and dissolution; the twenty-fifth, freed from creation and dissolution, is knowledge.
Learn from one another in order that ignorance, dear, as told by the sages, as the illustration of this Sankhya.
Knowledge belongs to all the senses of action: the sense of knowledge is held to be intellect; and the particulars of the senses of knowledge, so we have heard.
The wise call the mind the knowledge of the particulars; the five elements of the mind they call knowledge.
Of the five elements ego is the knowledge, without doubt; and of ego, intellect is the knowledge, lord of men.
Of intellect, nature, the unmanifest, supreme lord of the principles: knowledge is to be known, best of men, and the rule is held supreme.
Beyond the unmanifest they call the twenty-fifth knowledge; "all of all" is said of the knowable of knowledge, lord of the earth.
Knowledge is called the unmanifest, and the knowable is the twenty-fifth; likewise knowledge is the unmanifest, and the knower is the twenty-fifth.
These two, without beginning or end, are both held to be lords; both are called principle by the thinkers on knowledge.
From its law of creation and dissolution they call the unmanifest imperishable; it modifies again and again for the creation of qualities.
Of the qualities beginning with the great, one arises from another; because of presiding they call this the field, that the twenty-fifth.
When one draws the net of qualities into the unmanifest self, then the twenty-fifth dissolves with those qualities.
Qualities dissolve in qualities, then nature is one; and when, dear, the knower of the field also dissolves in that field,
then nature, called the qualities, goes to imperishability, and, Vaideha, to being without qualities, by turning back in the qualities.
So, at the destruction of the knowledge of the field, the knower of the field is without qualities by nature: so we have heard.
When this one becomes perishable, he then knows nature as having qualities, and the self's being without qualities.
Then he becomes pure by avoiding nature, when the wise one understands, "I am one, she is another."
Then he goes to separateness and does not come to mixture; and with nature, king of kings, he is not seen mixed and other.
But when he finds the net of qualities of nature disgusting, and sees another, then seeing he does not burn.

What have I done all this time, who like a fish through ignorance followed the net, this people?
mahabharata:12:295.24	Through delusion I followed one and another, people after people, like a fish following the water here from ignorance.
mahabharata:12:295.25	As a fish through ignorance does not think itself other than water, so I through ignorance did not know otherness.
mahabharata:12:295.26	Shame on me, unawake, who again followed this sunk one through delusion, one and another, people after people.
mahabharata:12:295.27	Let this be my kinsman here: with him is liberation; he has come to equality and oneness; as he is, so am I.
mahabharata:12:295.28	I see sameness here; I am like him; for he is stainless and manifest; so am I.
mahabharata:12:295.29	I who through ignorance and delusion acted with that ignorant one, I who am unattached stayed this long with the attached one.
mahabharata:12:295.30	Under her power I did not know this time; how shall I dwell with her among high, middle and low?
mahabharata:12:295.31	How shall I live with her who is the same with this one here? I shall go; from unawakeness this is the time to be steady.
mahabharata:12:295.32	I shall not go to dwelling together, for this long I was deceived; I am deceived by her, the modifier, I who am unmodified.
mahabharata:12:295.33	It is not her offence; the offence is mine, that I became attached here, turned toward her facing away.
mahabharata:12:295.34	Then I stood among many-formed shapes, the formless one, and the formless became of form, overcome by the sense of mine.
mahabharata:12:295.35	By the otherness of nature, in these and those wombs here, what was done by mine-ness for one without mine-ness, I who was in those and those wombs with a mind with lost awareness?
mahabharata:12:295.36	I have no business with her, made of ego, who having made herself many again joins me. Now I am awake, without mine-ness, without ego.
mahabharata:12:295.37	Leaving her, whose mine-ness is ever made of ego, I shall take refuge in the free of disease.
mahabharata:12:295.38	I shall go to equality with this one, not with her, the unconscious; peace is mine with him; there is no oneness with her.

So the twenty-fifth, by supreme awakening, awakens; he would restrain imperishability, giving up the perishable free of disease; seeing the unmanifest first, with the nature of the manifest, with qualities and without qualities, he becomes of that kind, Maithila.
This illustration of the imperishable and perishable has been told to you; the great knowledge here is by illustration of scripture.
I shall tell you further what is free of doubt, subtle, awakened and stainless; learn it as it has been heard.
Sankhya and yoga have been told by me by illustration from two shastras; the shastra told by Sankhya is the same as the vision of yoga.
The knowledge that awakens belongs to the Sankhyas, lord of the earth; it is told plainly there, wishing the good of disciples.
The skilled say that shastra is large; and in this shastra for the yogis, again curds, again the skull.
The twenty-fifth is the supreme principle; the lord of men does not see it; but the supreme of the Sankhyas is rightly described there.
The awake, the unawake and the awakening, in truth: the awakening and the awake: this they call the illustration of yoga."
[Vasishtha said:] "Constantly, for play, nature here modifies, lord of men, making the self many, and sees those same.
One awakening does not awaken to this modifier; and from awakening the unmanifest they say the awakening one.
But the unmanifest, with or without qualities, is never awakened; sometimes they call it the unawakened.
If this twenty-fifth awakens the unmanifest, then, awakening, he is of the nature of attachment: so scripture says.
By this they say "the imperishable unmanifest is unawakened"; and from awakening the unmanifest they say he is awakening.
Nor does he awaken the great-souled twenty-fifth; the twenty-sixth is stainless, awake, immeasurable and eternal.
Constantly the twenty-fifth and twenty-fourth are awakened; both of great radiance follow the visible and invisible.
The unmanifest, but not that Brahman, is awakened, dear, only; he does not see the lone twenty-fifth and twenty-fourth.
And when he awakens the supreme, pure, spotless intellect, tiger among kings, the twenty-sixth then attains awakeness.
Then he gives up the unmanifest, subject to creation and dissolution; the one without qualities knows nature as endowed with qualities and unconscious.
Then he is of the nature of aloneness, from seeing the unmanifest; joined with the alone, freed, he would reach the self.
They call this the principle; the unprincipled is ageless and deathless; by resting on the principles, this is principled, honoured one; the wise declare twenty-five principles.
He is not principled, dear; the wise one is unprincipled; he soon gives up the principle; that is the mark of the awakened.
I am the twenty-sixth: so the wise one, being grasped, ageless and deathless, by his sole strength goes to equality; there is no doubt.
By the awakened twenty-sixth even the one awakening is unwise; this is called manyness, by the illustration of Sankhya scripture.
Joined with the conscious, and the twenty-fifth, he becomes one with him, when he is not awakened by intellect.
Awakening, he goes to equality with the unawakened, Maithila; he is of the nature of attachment and the unattached self, lord of men.

Reaching the unattached self they know the unborn twenty-sixth; the pervader gives up the unmanifest when he awakens to this, the twenty-fourth, the unfathomable, by the awakening of the twenty-sixth.

This one is the unawakened and the awakening, sinless one, and the awake is told in truth, as by the illustration of scripture; this much of manyness and oneness is to be seen by those with the vision of shastra.
As gnat and fig-tree are separate, so are these two; as fish in water, so separateness is perceived.
So the manyness and oneness of these two is to be understood; this is called liberation, joined with knowledge of the unmanifest.
The one who dwells in bodies of this twenty-fifth is to be freed, they say, from the sphere of the unmanifest.
He is freed so, not otherwise: so it is settled; meeting the supreme he becomes of supreme nature.
Of pure nature, with the pure and awake he is wise; of freed nature, meeting the freed, bull among men.
With one engaged in duty he becomes engaged in duty; with one seeking liberation, liberation is met and so he would become.
Pure in deed and pure, he becomes of immeasurable radiance; of stainless soul, meeting the stainless soul.
Of lone soul, meeting the lone; independent, meeting the independent, he gains independence.
So much has been told to you by me, great king, true, the truth as it is; accepting the meaning without envy, the eternal, pure, primal Brahman.
This supreme should not be given by you to a man not devoted to the Veda, king; it is the teaching to be given to one who wishes to know, who bows in order to awaken.
It is not to be given likewise to one of false self, the crafty, the weak, the crooked-minded, or one who torments the knowledge of the learned; it is to be given by you to one such as I describe:
to the faithful, virtuous, one ever turned away from slander, of pure yoga and wise, active, patient and well-wishing,
to one of solitary character who loves rules, free of quarrel, much learned, discerning, patient with no harm, able in self-control and the peace of embodied beings.
To one lowest in these virtues it should not be given; they call this the supreme pure Brahman; one who gives to an unfit vessel will not be joined with the good, an expounder of dharma.
Even if one were to give this whole earth full of jewels, this should not be given to one without vows; to the master of senses, without doubt, this supreme may be given, lord of men.
Karala, let there be no fear in you; this supreme Brahman has been heard by you today, rightly told, supremely holy, griefless, utterly without beginning or middle.
Birth and death are unfathomable, king, free of disease, fearless and auspicious; seeing this, give up all delusion today, having known the truth of the meaning of knowledge.
This was obtained long ago from the eternal Hiranyagarbha, as he told, lord of men; having appeased by effort that one of fierce splendour, the eternal Brahman, as you have asked.
As you have asked me, lord of men, so this has been told to you by me today; and so I received from Brahma the great and ancient knowledge of the knowers of liberation, lord of men."
[Bhishma said:] "This has been told, the supreme Brahman, from which one does not return again, the twenty-fifth, great king, by the illustration of the supreme sages.
He who has reached the supreme knowledge returns again; and he does not awaken in truth; the awakening is ageless and deathless.
This is the best of knowledges, bringing the highest good, told to you by me in truth, dear, having heard it from the divine sage, king.
From Hiranyagarbha to the sage Vasishtha, the great soul; from Vasishtha, tiger among sages, Narada received this.
From Narada this eternal Brahman was known to me; do not grieve, lord of the Kurus, hearing this supreme state.
One who has known the perishable and imperishable has no fear; but fear is his, lord of the earth, who does not know this.
From ignorance the deluded self, suffering again and again, after death gains thousands of births ending in death.
He gains the world of the gods, and animal birth and human birth, if he is purified in time from that ocean of ignorance.
The ocean of ignorance is dreadful, unmanifest, called unfathomable, in which beings sink day by day, Bharata.
Since you have crossed from that unfathomable, unmanifest, eternal one, you are therefore free of dust and darkness, lord of the earth."
[Bhishma said:] Seated, attended, bowing his head to the sage, afterward with his permission, Vasuman asked this:
Blessed one, what is this good that may be for a man here or hereafter in the impermanent body, under the power of desire?
Honoured and asked, the great-souled one of great austerity then spoke to him these words that bring the good:

You wish for what is not contrary to the mind hereafter and here; turn away, with restrained senses, from what is contrary to beings.
mahabharata:12:297.6	Dharma is beneficial to the good among men, and dharma is the support of the good; from dharma the three worlds, moving and unmoving, go on.
mahabharata:12:297.7	You who are fond of the sweet and desirous, why do you not go to freedom from craving? You see the honey, ill-minded; you do not see the fall.
mahabharata:12:297.8	As practice must be made in knowledge by one wishing its fruit, so practice must be made in dharma by one wishing its fruit.
mahabharata:12:297.9	Pure action is hard for the bad man who wishes dharma; but for the good man who wishes dharma, an easy action is hard.
mahabharata:12:297.14	Non-cruel, pure, self-controlled, truthful in speech, standing in honesty, with pure origin and deed, a twice-born knower of the Veda is a fit vessel.
mahabharata:12:297.15	The honoured only wife, by birth, is held the womb here; the learned master of Rik, Yajus and Saman, of good deed, is called a fit vessel.
mahabharata:12:297.16	That is dharma and that adharma, for each man, according to the particular deed of the vessel, observing place and time.
mahabharata:12:297.17	As a man might wipe a little dust from his body playfully, but removing sin takes great effort,
mahabharata:12:297.18	as ghee is medicine for one who has purged well, so for one whose faults are removed, dharma brings happiness hereafter.
mahabharata:12:297.19	The mind in all beings acts in good and bad; having drawn it from the bad, one should lower it into the good.
mahabharata:12:297.20	Honour all that is done everywhere in every way; wherever your attachment is, let dharma be made in your own dharma as you wish.
mahabharata:12:297.21	Unsteady one, stand in steadiness; ill-minded one, become wise; unquiet one, be calm; unwise one, act like the wise.
mahabharata:12:297.22	It can be reached by energy, joined with means; the good here and hereafter has steadiness as its supreme root.
mahabharata:12:297.23	The royal sage Mahabhisha, lacking steadiness, fell from heaven, and Yayati, his merit spent, regained worlds through steadiness.
mahabharata:12:297.24	By serving ascetics, the righteous and the learned, you will gain vast understanding and will reach the good.
He, endowed with good nature, hearing the sage's words, turned his mind from desire and set his understanding on dharma.
[Yudhishthira said:] "What is auspicious, constant, fearless, constant, imperishable, undecaying, pure, constant and without effort: you should tell it."
[Bhishma said:] "Here I shall relate to you an ancient tale, the dialogue of Yajnavalkya and Janaka, Bharata.
King Janaka, son of Devarata, best of those who ask questions, asked the best of sages, Yajnavalkya, a question, for fame.
'How many senses are there, brahmana sage, how many natures are remembered? What is the unmanifest, the supreme Brahman, and what is beyond that?
You should tell the origin and the dissolution and the reckoning of time too, best of brahmins, to me who desire your favour.
I ask out of ignorance, for you are a treasury made of knowledge; I wish to hear all this without doubt.'
[Yajnavalkya said:] 'Hear, lord of the earth, what you ask: the supreme knowledge of the yogis and especially of the Sankhyas.
Nothing is unknown to you; you ask me; and what is asked must be told; this is eternal dharma.
These are the eight natures; hear from me the modifications also: ear, skin, eye, tongue and nose as fifth,
sound, touch, form, taste and smell, speech, hands, feet, anus and genital:
these are the particulars, king of kings, in the five great elements; and these are the senses of knowledge with their particulars, Maithila.
The thinkers on the course of the self call the mind sixteenfold; you and other learned ones, expert in the intellect of principles, know it.
From the unmanifest the great self arises, lord of the earth; this the wise call the first creation, the primary.
And from the great ego arises, lord of men; they call this the second creation, held to be of the nature of intellect.
From ego the mind arises, of the nature of the qualities of elements; this is the third creation, called the egoistic.
From the mind the great elements arise, lord of men; they call this the fourth creation, the mental.
Sound, touch, form, taste and smell as fifth: the thinkers on beings call this the fifth creation, the elemental.
Ear, skin, eye, tongue and nose as fifth: they call this the sixth creation, held to be of the nature of much thought.
The group of ear-sense below arises, lord of men; they call this the seventh creation, held the sensory.
The upward current and the sideways arises, lord of men; they call this the eighth creation, the wise call it the straight.
The sideways current and the downward current arises, lord of men; they call this the ninth creation, the wise call it the straight.
These nine creations and the principles, lord of men, are told as twenty-four, by the illustration of scripture.
Beyond this, great king, learn from me in truth the reckoning of time of this quality as told by great souls.'"
[Yajnavalkya said:] "Night is as long, lord of men; awakened, he first creates the herbs, the life of all embodied beings.
Then he created Brahma, born of the golden egg; that is the form of all beings: so we have heard.
Having dwelt a year in the egg, the great sage came out and set half the whole earth and half heaven, as Prajapati.
Of heaven and earth, king, so it is read in the Vedas; between the two halves the lord made space.
The reckoning of this by the masters of the Veda and its limbs: ten thousand aeons, less a quarter, is said to be a day, and the thinkers on the self say night is as long.
The sage creates ego, a divine-natured being, and four other sons from his body earlier, the great sage; they are heard to be ancestors of the ancestors, best of kings.
The gods are sons of the ancestors, and the worlds are covered by the gods, moving and unmoving, best of men: so we have heard.
The supreme ego created beings in five ways: earth, wind, space, water and light as fifth.
They say the night of this one making the third here, in five thousand aeons, and a day is as long.
Sound, touch, form, taste and smell as fifth: these are the particulars, king of kings, in the five great elements, by which beings are filled day by day, lord of the earth.
They covet one another, devoted to one another's good, they think one another, and compete with one another.
Mutually struck by captivating qualities, imperishable, they turn about right here, entering animal wombs.
Three thousand aeons is their day, and the night of mind is as long, lord of men.
The mind moves, king of kings, and all is moved by the senses; the senses do not see; the mind alone sees here.
The eye sees forms, but by the mind, not by the eye; when the mind is distracted the eye, though looking, does not see; so they say all the senses see.
When the mind ceases, king, the senses cease; but when the senses cease the mind does not cease; thus one should understand the senses as led by the mind.
The mind is called the lord of all the senses, greatly famous one; all beings enter this."
[Yajnavalkya said:] "As he gathers creatures and creates them again and again, Brahma is without beginning or end, eternal and imperishable.
Knowing the end of day, and with mind asleep at night, he urged the blessed one: 'I am the unmanifest; I made man.'
Then the sun of a hundred thousand rays, urged by the unmanifest, making himself twelvefold, blazed like fire.
With his energy he burns up quickly the net of fourfold creatures: womb-born, egg-born, sweat-born and sprout-born, lord of men.
By the mere opening of the eyes the unmoving and moving are destroyed; the earth becomes like a tortoise's back on every side.
Having burnt the world, he of immeasurable strength, the earth alone is quickly filled on all sides by strong water.
Then, reaching the fire of time, that water goes to destruction; when the water is destroyed, king of kings, the great fire blazes.
That immeasurable, very strong blazing fire, the heat of all beings, with seven flames, the wind swiftly...
Even that incomparable self, the universe, Shambhu, Prajapati, with minuteness, lightness and attainment, the lord, the imperishable light,
has hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads and faces everywhere, ears everywhere in the world; he stands covering all.
The heart of all beings, of the size of a thumb at the joint, the great soul, the lord of the universe, swallows the endless.
Then everything came to be, imperishable, undecaying, unwounded; the maker of past, future and men, the blameless.
This dissolution of yours, king of kings, has been told properly; hear the self, the elements and the gods."
[Yajnavalkya said:] "The anus is the self-level, say those who see the truth of the meaning; excretion is its element, Mitra the deity there.
The organ is the self-level, as the illustration of yoga; bliss is its element, and Prajapati the deity.
The hands are the self-level, as the illustration of Sankhya; doing is the element, and Indra the deity there.
Speech is the self-level, as the illustration of scripture; speaking is the element, and Fire the deity there.
The eye is the self-level, as the illustration of scripture; form is the element there, and the Sun the deity.
The ear is the self-level, as the illustration of scripture; sound is the element there, and the directions the deity.
The tongue is the self-level, as the illustration of truth; taste is the element, and the waters the deity.
The nose is the self-level, as the illustration of scripture; smell is the element, and Earth the deity.
The egoistic is the self-level, as the illustration of principle; conceit is the element, and Bhava the deity there.
Intellect is the self-level, as the illustration of the Veda; the knowable is the element, and the knower of the field the deity there.
This glory has been described to you as manifest, king, in the beginning, middle and end, as the knower of truth in truth.
Nature modifies the qualities at will, from her own desire, for play, great king, by hundreds and thousands.
As thousands of lamps are lit from a lamp for a purpose, so nature modifies many qualities of the Person.
Sattva: bliss, abundance, joy and clarity, happiness, purity, health, contentment, faith,
freedom from meanness, from violent effort, forbearance, steadiness, non-violence, equanimity, truth, freedom from debt, gentleness, modesty, freedom from restlessness,
purity, honesty, good conduct, freedom from greed, heart's freedom from confusion, not boasting of the loss of wished and unwished things done,
favour by giving, concern for others without desire for gain, and compassion for all beings: these are held to be the qualities of sattva.
The aggregate of the qualities of rajas: form, lordship, strife, excessive eating, lack of compassion, resort to pleasure and pain,
delight in slander, resort to disputes, ego, disrespect, worry, resort to enmity,
torment, theft, loss of shame, dishonesty, division and harshness, desire, anger, intoxication, pride, hatred and over-speech: these are said to be the qualities of rajas.
I shall tell the aggregate of the tamasic; understand it: delusion, lack of light, Tamisra, called Andhatamisra,
death and Andhatamisra; Tamisra is said to be anger; the marks of tamas here are liking for food,
never being satisfied with meals, insatiety in drink, keeping scents and garments in pleasures, in beds and seats,
delight in sleep by day, in dispute, in heedlessness, in dance, music and song; faith from ignorance, hatred of special dharmas: these are the qualities of tamas."
[Yajnavalkya said:] "By hundreds, thousands and hundreds of thousands, and by crores, this one makes the inner self by the self.
The highest place is of the sattvic, the middle here is of the rajasic, the lowest place is of the tamasic, say the thinkers on the self.
By pure merit alone he gains an upward goal; by merit and sin, human birth; by adharma, a downward goal.
Learn from me in truth the pairing and meeting of these three, sattva, rajas and tamas.
Rajas is seen in sattva, tamas in rajas, sattva in tamas, and the unmanifest in sattva.
Joined with unmanifest sattva one would reach the world of the gods; joined with rajas and sattva he is born among men.
Joined with rajas and tamas he is born in animal wombs; joined with rajas, tamas and sattva he would reach humanity.
For those freed from merit and sin the wise speak of a place that is eternal, imperishable, undecaying and fearless."
The king asked the blessed Vibhavasu for a fee: "May you be ever present here, Chitrabhanu." The blessed Agni said to the king, "So be it."
You are lord of beings, in you the worlds are founded; you are the slayer of Namuchi, of Vishvarupa and of Bala.
He by whom Bhimasena's iron image was ground to powder long ago, a strong man, took refuge with a woman for strength.
Savyasachi will come to this city; he will release you from sorrow, best of men. Then Keshava went and saw Rama, alone in a lonely place in the forest.
While Indra thus spoke to Yudhishthira, lord of the Kurus, Dharma in bodily form himself spoke to his own son.
